title: EDF Schedulability Analysis on Mixed-Criticality Systems with Permitted Failure Probability

extraction.paper_name: EDF Schedulability Analysis on Mixed-Criticality Systems with Permitted Failure Probability
extraction.paper_description: This paper extends the mixed-criticality task model by incorporating a failure probability parameter for each task and a system-level permitted failure probability. It introduces a clustering-based scheduling algorithm (LFF-Clustering) and a corresponding EDF-based schedulability test that leverages probabilistic information to reduce pessimism in mixed-criticality analysis.

formal_description.statement: A Mixed-Criticality (MC) task instance I is defined as I = (tau, F_S), where tau = {tau_1, tau_2, ..., tau_n} is a set of tasks and F_S is the permitted system failure probability per hour. Each HI-criticality task tau_i is represented as ([c_i_LO, c_i_HI], f_i, p_i, chi_i).

variables.tau: The set of n tasks in the system
variables.f_i: Probability of any job of tau_i exceeding c_i_LO within one hour
variables.p_i: Period and implicit deadline of task i
variables.chi_i: Criticality level of task i (LO or HI)

assumptions: f_i is derived from probabilistic WCET (pWCET) distributions
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the formal structure of a probabilistic mixed-criticality task system.

informal_sketch.intuition: A system is defined not just by its timing constraints, but by how often it is allowed to fail. Each high-importance task has a known probability of needing more than its 'normal' (LO) execution time.
steps: Identify the set of tasks and their criticality levels
For HI tasks, specify two execution bounds and the probability of exceeding the lower one
Set a global safety target F_S for the entire system
key_insights: Moves from deterministic 'worst-case' to a probabilistic 'acceptable-risk' model

formal_description.statement: A task set is 'strongly probabilistic schedulable' if the probability of missing ANY deadline is < F_S. It is 'weakly probabilistic schedulable' if the probability of missing any HI-criticality deadline is < F_S.
assumptions: All deadlines are met if no job exceeds its c_i_LO
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the success criteria for the scheduling strategy.

informal_sketch.intuition: Strong schedulability protects everyone (LO and HI tasks) within the risk budget. Weak schedulability only guarantees the important (HI) tasks within that budget.
steps: Determine if the probability of any task missing a deadline is within F_S
If yes, the system is strongly schedulable
If only HI tasks are guaranteed within F_S, it is weakly schedulable
key_insights: Allows for different levels of service guarantee based on criticality

formal_description.statement: The additional utilization cost delta_i of a HI-criticality task tau_i is delta_i = (c_i_HI - c_i_LO) / p_i.

variables.delta_i: Additional utilization required if task i enters HI-mode

formal_description.conclusion: Quantifies the extra processor capacity needed to handle a task's execution overrun.

informal_sketch.intuition: This represents the 'extra' percentage of the processor a task needs if it exceeds its normal execution time.
steps: Calculate the difference between the conservative and optimistic execution times
Divide by the period to get the utilization impact
key_insights: Isolates the 'risk' component of task utilization

formal_description.statement: The failure probability g_m of a cluster G_m is the probability that more than one task in the cluster exceeds its c_i_LO within an hour: g_m = 1 - product_{i in G_m}(1 - f_i) - sum_{j in G_m}(f_j * product_{i in G_m, i != j}(1 - f_i)).

variables.G_m: The set of tasks assigned to cluster m

assumptions: Tasks within a cluster are independent
formal_description.conclusion: Calculates the risk that the cluster's provisioned capacity (which only covers one task overrun) will be exceeded.

informal_sketch.intuition: A cluster is designed to handle exactly one task exceeding its LO-WCET. It 'fails' if two or more tasks exceed their LO-WCETs simultaneously.
steps: Calculate the probability that NO tasks exceed their LO-WCET
Calculate the probability that EXACTLY ONE task exceeds its LO-WCET
Subtract both from 1 to find the probability of 2 or more overruns
key_insights: Clustering allows sharing 'extra' capacity among multiple tasks, provided the probability of multiple simultaneous overruns is low

formal_description.statement: If g_m < F_S / M holds for every cluster G_m (where M is the total number of clusters), then the probability of having no failure in any cluster is greater than (1 - F_S).
formal_description.conclusion: Provides a sufficient condition to bound the total system risk using per-cluster thresholds.

informal_sketch.intuition: If we keep the risk in each of the M clusters very small (less than F_S/M), the combined risk across the whole system stays below F_S.
steps: Divide the total allowed risk F_S by the number of clusters M
Ensure each cluster's internal failure probability g_m is below this threshold
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def is_cluster_risk_acceptable(g_m, F_S, M):
    return g_m < (F_S / M)
key_insights: Uses the Binomial Theorem/Union Bound logic to aggregate independent risks

formal_description.statement: The Largest Fit First (LFF) Clustering algorithm partitions HI-criticality tasks into M clusters to minimize total additional utilization delta_total = sum_{m=1 to M}(max_{i in G_m} delta_i) while satisfying g_m < F_S / M.

variables.delta_total: Total additional utilization provisioned for the system

formal_description.conclusion: Produces a value delta_total used for schedulability testing.

informal_sketch.intuition: Sort tasks by their 'extra' utilization needs. Try to pack tasks into existing clusters to 'hide' their extra utilization under the largest task in that cluster, as long as the risk of multiple overruns stays low.
steps: Sort HI tasks by delta_i descending
For each task, try to fit it into an existing cluster without violating the risk bound g_m < F_S/M
If it doesn't fit anywhere, create a new cluster
The total extra utilization is the sum of the largest delta_i in each cluster
key_insights: Greedy approach: tasks with smaller delta_i are 'absorbed' into clusters of tasks with larger delta_i for free

formal_description.statement: If no job exceeds its c_i_LO, then no deadline is missed if delta_total * (1 - sum_{i in HI} c_i_LO / p_i) + sum_{i=1 to n} c_i_LO / p_i <= 1.
assumptions: System is feasible when no job exceeds c_i_LO
A server task with utilization delta_total and period 1 is used
formal_description.conclusion: Provides a sufficient condition for LO-mode schedulability when a HI-mode server is present.

informal_sketch.intuition: Even if we reserve capacity (a server) for HI-mode overruns, we must ensure that in normal operation (LO-mode), the combination of regular tasks and the server doesn't exceed the processor capacity.
steps: Calculate total LO-mode utilization U_LO_total
Calculate HI-task LO-mode utilization U_HI_LO
Check the weighted inequality involving delta_total
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def check_theorem_1(tasks, delta_total):
    U_LO_total = sum(t.c_LO / t.p for t in tasks)
    U_HI_LO = sum(t.c_LO / t.p for t in tasks if t.chi == 'HI')
    
    condition = delta_total * (1 - U_HI_LO) + U_LO_total
    return condition <= 1.0
key_insights: The server only consumes its full budget when HI-tasks are active, allowing LO-tasks to utilize the remaining slack

formal_description.statement: The pMC schedulability test is sufficient: 1) If sum_{i=1 to n} (c_i_LO / p_i) + delta_total <= 1, it is strongly probabilistic schedulable. 2) If sum_{i in HI} (c_i_LO / p_i) + delta_total <= 1 AND Theorem 1 holds, it is weakly probabilistic schedulable.
formal_description.conclusion: Formalizes the complete schedulability test logic.

informal_sketch.intuition: The test checks two scenarios. First, can we fit everyone plus the risk-buffer? If so, strong success. If not, can we at least fit the important tasks plus the risk-buffer, while ensuring normal mode still works? If so, weak success.
steps: Run LFF-Clustering to get delta_total
Check if (Total LO Utilization + delta_total) <= 1
If failed, check if (HI-only LO Utilization + delta_total) <= 1 AND Theorem 1 condition
key_insights: Combines deterministic utilization bounds with the probabilistic clustering results
